verdict_text:
YES

The script matches the spec on every point I can check from reading: it loads all three checkpoints, asserts identical key sets, and bit-exact equality (`torch.equal`) of every non-MLP tensor against the base before writing anything; the regex `fullmatch` selects exactly the four MLP tensor names per layer; both task vectors are taken against the unmodified `base` (`out` is a separate dict, and `b` is re-read from `base` each iteration), so there is no ordering hazard; arithmetic is done in float32 and cast back to `base[name].dtype` (float16); all other entries come from `dict(base)` unchanged with unchanged names; and it asserts `merged == 64` and `len(out) == 244` before saving to `out/T4/model.safetensors`.

Two things I could not verify from the artifact alone: the behaviour of the imported `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper (not shown here), and that `assert` is used for the "fail loudly" checks, which would be silently skipped if the script were ever run under `python -O` — under the prescribed `python out/T4/solution.py` invocation this is not an issue.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
